security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates WMACC/WMACCU on RV64 without enforcing XLEN==32 check (REQUIRE_32BIT), causing OP-IMM-32 opcode collision with RV64 ADDIW/SLLIW/SRLIW/SRAIW — an illegal instruction on RV64 per spec is executed as a valid widening multiply-accumulate, or vice versa, producing wrong register state
affected_entities: TCG gen_gpr for x0/x1 pair on rd_p=0
security_spec.summary: WMACC/WMACCU are RV32-only but reuse OP-IMM-32 opcode space owned by RV64 ADDIW-family; missing XLEN gating in QEMU TCG decode causes instruction confusion between widening MAC and 32-bit integer ops, corrupting guest register state and enabling guest-to-host escape via wrong-code execution

findings.finding: OP-IMM-32 decode table (addiw/slliw/srliw/sraiw) contains no P-ext WMACC entries. No collision exists between standard RV64 word instructions and any widening multiply-accumulate instructions, because P-ext wmacc is not implemented at all.

All vwmacc/vwmaccsu/vwmaccus instructions use opcode space 1010111 (OP-V), not 0011011 (OP-IMM-32). No encoding collision with RV64 ADDIW/SLLIW/SRLIW/SRAIW. The vector check functions (require_rvv + vext_check_isa_ill) correctly gate execution.

REQUIRE_32BIT macro exists and correctly returns false when get_xl(ctx) != MXL_RV32. It is currently used by rev8_32, fmvh_x_d/fmvp_d_x, and Zilsd instructions. Not applicable to wmacc because no P-ext wmacc translator functions exist to use it.

No P-ext (Zpn/Zpsfoperand) config flags exist. If a PR adds P-ext WMACC instructions decoded via OP-IMM-32 without REQUIRE_32BIT + REQUIRE_EXT(Zpn), RV64 guests would execute these as valid when they should trigger illegal-instruction. The hypothetical risk is real but has no current code to exploit.

Vector wmacc translator functions properly use require_rvv() + vext_check_isa_ill() gates, which check RVV is enabled. These use OP-V opcode space and have no encoding overlap with OP-IMM-32. No XLEN enforcement is needed because the vector opcode space is distinct.
